Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 4, Verse 40

“The ignorant, the faithless, and the doubting one perish. For the doubting one there is neither this world nor the next, nor any happiness.”

The harshest line of the chapter, and its target is samshaya — not honest inquiry but the settled inability to commit. Perpetual doubt is described as costing everything.
